section_summary: This section concludes a Tokyo despatch on whether Japan’s tax system was discouraging foreign commercial entrants and investment. Its enclosures include Henry Shavell’s analysis of income, corporation, customs, and consumption taxes; a 1947 occupation directive on taxation of non-Japanese nationals; and tax reform proposals prepared by representatives of Standard-Vacuum Oil Company.

subfiles.title: Japanese Taxation of Commercial Entrants as Related to Attraction of Foreign Capital Investment to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports discussions of Japanese taxation of foreign businesses and recommends considering broad tax reform.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes objections to high Japanese taxes and a June 17 discussion of Shavell’s memorandum. The Mission favors general tax reform over preferential rates for foreign investors and forwards two memoranda.

subfiles.title: Japanese Taxation of Commercial Entrants
subfiles.about: Examines how Japanese taxes affect foreign commercial entrants and proposes courses of action for SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Shavell argues that steep personal and corporation taxes discourage foreign investment, while customs and consumption taxes on non-occupation imports are largely unenforced. He examines the effects of duty-free imported cigarettes and liquor on Japanese revenue and competition, and identifies problems with the non-yen income exemption under SCAPIN 4938-A. He favors broad reductions or revisions to income and excess profits taxes over preferential treatment for foreigners, alongside a review of import taxes and exemptions.

subfiles.title: Applicability of Taxes to Non-Japanese Nationals
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, signed by R. M. Levy
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sets limits on Japanese taxation of non-Japanese nationals and income received in non-yen currencies.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 4938-A permits nondiscriminatory taxation while exempting specified official salaries and lawfully received non-yen income.

subfiles.title: Proposals for Tax Legislation
subfiles.from: Representatives of Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Proposes changes to Japanese personal, corporation, prefectural, and local taxes affecting foreign firms.
subfiles.summary: The statement argues that high Japanese tax rates threaten foreign business operations. It proposes taxing foreign staff only on income received or remitted to Japan, clarifying corporate capital and income allocation rules, and removing business income taxation from prefectural and local governments.
